 Judgment

1. Originally, the present claim case was filed by the claimants under section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 in the year 2007 with the averments that on 19/20.03.2007, Sh. Mohan Chand Pant (deceased herein) along with his Conductor had driven his bus to the Mela at Kela Devi, Karoli,
Rajasthan and after parking his bus, he slept on the ground and later, at about 02:00 a.m. (night),
the Conductor found that driver of bus bearing registration no. RJ-27P-4855 (in short "offending vehicle") had crushed the deceased.
It was alleged that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was claimed that the deceased was the only bread earner of his family and all the petitioners were dependent upon him, thus, prayed for compensation.

2. This Tribunal held the enquiry proceedings and vide judgment dated 07.12.2012, my learned predecessor passed the award whereby petitioners (LRs of deceased Mohan Chand Pant) were granted a compensation of Rs.7,33,370/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum (except for the period not specifically allowed on the total compensation amount) from the date of filing of petition t i l l

_ company/ respondent no.4 was directed to pay the award amount with recovery rights against respondent no.1/ driver and respondent no.2/ owner of the offending vehicle, who had failed to prove on record that they were holding a valid Permit of the offending bus at the time of accident.

3. The award was challenged by New India Assurance Co. Ltd. (respondent no.4 herein) before Hon'ble Delhi High Court in appeal bearing MAC.APP. no. 165/2013, titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Devki & Ors.

sentences.text: In the appeal, insurance company raised questions about the propriety and correctness of the finding of facts concerning the involvement of the offending bus and negligence on the part of its driver.

Hon'ble High Court disposed of the appeal vide order dated 29.02.2016 wherein it was observed as under:
"9.

It is clear from the perusal of the evidence adduced before the Tribunal, and the view taken thereupon, that the claimants did not examine any witness, whether in the nature of eye-witness of the actual occurrence or of the circumstances attending upon the events leading to the death.
The version of the conductor Manoj Kumar in the FIR (Ex.PW1/1) is in the nature of his statement to the police under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.PC).
It is trite that a statement whether made under section 154 or section 161 Cr.PC cannot be treated as evidence in the strict senses of the term.
The said witness, it is conceded, has been available all along and could have been summoned to prove the circumstances.

It may be that there is no eye-witness available to the actual occurrences wherein the deceased went to sleep on the ground during the night near the Kela Devi fair and on next morning was found having been crushed by the offending bus.

But then, the circumstances in which the deceased had retired for the night, and the circumstances in which his dead body was found crushed under the wheels of the said bus at least could have been brought h o m e

In absence of the witnesses of such circumstances, the principle of res ipsa locutor also cannot be invoked on the available material brought before the Tribunal.
10. Faced with the above situation, the learned counsel for the claimants fairly conceded that the conclusions on facts reached by the Tribunal cannot be denied.

He submitted that since the conductor on whose statement the FIR had been registered has been available, in order not to deny just compensation to the next of kin of the deceased, justice demands that fresh opportunity be given to them to bring the said witness before the Tribunal.
The counsel submitted that while the appeal of the insurance company may be allowed, the claimants' case may be remitted to the Tribunal for further inquiry.
The counsel for the appellant insurance company submitted that he has nothing to say on this prayer.
11. In view of the above, the impugned judgment and award are set aside.
The matter is remitted to the Tribunal for further inquiry in accordance with law in the light of the above noted observations.
During the said further inquiry, the claimants shall be entitled to adduce further evidence.
Needless to add, the opposite parties are entitled to lead evidence in rebuttal.

The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal for aforesaid inquiry on 22.04.2016."
4.

After receiving the aforementioned order from the Hon'ble High Court, file was taken up by my learned predecessor on 22.04.2016, when only learned counsel for insurance company (respondent no.4 herein) was present and therefore, notice was issued to the petitioners to appear before this Tribunal on 19.05.2016 for further inquiry in terms of given directions.

Subsequently, when learned counsel for petitioners appeared on court- notice on 14.10.2016, my learned predecessor issued notices also to respondent nos. 1, 2 and 3, who were earlier proceeded against ex-parte, to appear on 2 3 . 1 1 . 2 0 1 6 .

____ respondent nos.1 and 3 remained unserved and since then, matter kept on adjourned for service of respondent nos. 1 and 3 and ultimately, efforts were made to get them served by way of publication.

However, respondent nos. 1 and 3 did not appear despite their service through publication in newspaper in Rashtriya Sahara dated 06.12.2018 and my learned predecessor proceeded against them ex-parte vide order dated 20.03.2019.

5. As per judicial record, thereafter, the petitioners were granted ample opportunities for producing/
examining eye-witness but the petitioners failed to lead evidence of the eye-witness despite the fact that while appearing before the Hon'ble High Court, they had conceded that eye-witness was available all along to prove the circumstances in which death of deceased occurred.

6. It is evident that the specific directions with which the matter was remitted to this Tribunal for further inquiry in accordance with law, have not been complied with by the petitioners, since they failed to examine the eye-witness as claimed by them before the Hon'ble High Court.

It was Devki vs Murari Lal on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72058115/
3 specifically observed by the Hon'ble High Court in the aforesaid order that in absence of evidence of the eye-witness, the principle of res ipsa locutor also cannot be invoked on the available material brought before the Tribunal.

In the circumstances, since no eye-witness has been examined by the petitioners in terms of directions of Hon'ble High Court and as such, principle of res ipsa lucutor is not applicable on the facts and circumstances of the present case as observed by Hon'ble High Court, it is held that the claim of petitioners that the death of deceased occurred due to rash and n e g l i g e n c e o n t h e p a r t o f d r i v e r o f t h e a l l e g e d o f f e n d i n g v e h i c l e ______________________________________________________________________ stands not proved on record

and accordingly, the instant claim petition is dismissed.
7. The case is disposed of in above terms.
